launch-in-indianapolis-white-river-state.summary: Downtown Indianapolis's 250-acre cultural park, linking riverfront greenspaces, the Canal Walk, museums, zoo, amphitheater, ballpark and trails.
launch-in-indianapolis-white-river-state.hours: Park grounds and the Canal Walk are open daily 5:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. Museums, zoo, rentals, concerts and visitor facilities keep separate hours.
launch-in-indianapolis-white-river-state.parking: The underground park garage charges by duration, currently beginning at $10 for up to two hours; special-event rates can differ. Downtown garages and meters are alternatives.
launch-in-indianapolis-white-river-state.arrival: Choose the Canal, zoo, museums, amphitheater, Military Park or Celebration Plaza before entering the district; attractions span both sides of the river.
launch-in-indianapolis-white-river-state.restrooms: Reliable restrooms are inside attractions during their operating hours; outdoor event and visitor facilities vary.
launch-in-indianapolis-white-river-state.cost: Park greenspaces and Canal Walk are free. Garage parking, museums, zoo, rentals, concerts and sporting events charge separately.
launch-in-indianapolis-white-river-state.accessibility: Paved promenades, ramps, bridges and attraction entrances provide broad access, but event closures and elevator outages can alter routes.
launch-in-indianapolis-white-river-state.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in ordinary outdoor park spaces; attractions and ticketed events set their own animal policies.
launch-in-indianapolis-white-river-state.family: The free Canal Walk and lawns can be combined with a paid zoo or museum visit; do not assume one attraction ticket covers another.
launch-in-indianapolis-white-river-state.transit: IndyGo routes, downtown bike infrastructure and the Cultural Trail reach the park from central Indianapolis.
launch-in-indianapolis-white-river-state.need: This is an attraction district, not one single park stop. Confirm each venue's hours and tickets, and check official bridge, trail and event closure notices before arrival.

launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.address: 5700 North Eagle Creek Parkway, Indianapolis, IN 46254
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.summary: One of the country's largest city parks, with a 1,400-acre reservoir, 3,900 acres of forest, two nature centers, beach, marina, trails, birding and dog recreation.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.hours: Park hours are dawn to dusk. The Earth Discovery Center and Ornithology Center are open Tuesday-Saturday 10:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m., Sunday 1:00-5:00 p.m., and closed Monday.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.parking: Enter at 5700 North Eagle Creek Parkway or 7100 North Eagle Creek Parkway. Vehicle admission includes parking; use the entrance closest to your selected destination.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.arrival: Use the 56th Street entrance for many central facilities or the 71st Street entrance from I-65. Beach, marina and nature centers are separated around the reservoir.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.restrooms: Restrooms serve nature centers, beach, marina and developed picnic areas; remote trails have limited facilities.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.cost: Current day rates are $6 per resident vehicle, $8 per nonresident vehicle, or $1 per hiker or bicyclist. Boat launch, rentals, Go Ape and reservations cost extra.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.accessibility: Nature centers and developed areas offer accessible routes; wooded trails, shorelines and older facilities vary. Pin Oak Trail accessibility upgrades are underway.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed under park rules, with off-leash use limited to the fee-based Canine Companion Zone.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.family: Nature centers, playgrounds and the seasonal swimming beach can fill a day. Check beach status and center schedules before departure.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.transit: Public transit is limited at the park entrances; driving or cycling is most practical.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.need: Pay the entrance fee once and keep the receipt if re-entry is permitted that day. Swimming, boating and aerial adventure depend on weather, staffing and seasonal operations.

launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.summary: Indianapolis's oldest city park, with conservatory, sunken gardens, pagoda, arts and family centers, aquatic center, amphitheater, courts, playgrounds and trails.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.hours: Outdoor grounds are generally available daily. The Family Center currently operates Monday-Friday 11:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. and is closed weekends; every major facility keeps its own schedule.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.parking: Free lots serve Pagoda Drive, Conservatory Drive, the family center and aquatic center. Concerts, exhibitions and pool days can fill the nearest spaces.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.arrival: Route to the Conservatory and Sunken Garden, Pagoda, Aquatic Center, Arts Center, MacAllister Amphitheater or Family Center rather than the general park pin.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.restrooms: Reliable restrooms are inside staffed facilities during their hours; outdoor and event facilities vary.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.cost: Park grounds, Sunken Garden and Arts Center galleries are generally free. Conservatory admission is currently $4; pool, programs, events and reservations may charge.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.accessibility: Developed attractions have paved approaches, though historic structures, garden grades and trail surfaces vary.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in ordinary outdoor spaces but not inside the conservatory, aquatic center or other restricted facilities.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.family: The conservatory, gardens, pagoda and seasonal pool offer very different visits; pair facilities only after checking each schedule.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.transit: IndyGo service and the Pleasant Run Trail connect the near-southside park with surrounding neighborhoods.
launch-in-indianapolis-garfield-park.need: The Conservatory and Sunken Garden are closed Monday and normally open Tuesday-Saturday 10:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. and Sunday 1:00-5:00 p.m. Inclement weather can close the garden. The restored Sunken Garden fountains reopened in June 2026.

launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.summary: A 95-acre White River nature park with landmark Ruins, a nature center, newly rebuilt inclusive playground, arboretum, gardens, prairie and two miles of wooded trails.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.hours: Park grounds are open dawn to dusk. The Nature Center is open Monday-Saturday 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.parking: Free parking is available near the playground, west of the Ruins and by the Nature Center. Choose the destination before entering.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.arrival: The Ruins, Nature Center and playground form the developed core; trail descents toward the White River begin beyond it.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.restrooms: The Nature Center provides the most reliable facilities during its hours; playground and event-area facilities may vary.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.cost: Park, Ruins, playground, trails and Nature Center general access are free. Programs, rentals and concerts may charge.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.accessibility: The 2025 playground, entry court and connecting walks were designed for inclusive access; wooded ravine trails remain natural and uneven.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome on outdoor paths under posted rules; they are not allowed in all buildings or play areas.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.family: The $6 million nature-themed playground opened in November 2025 and has age-separated, inclusive play areas. The Nature Center is an excellent indoor complement.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.transit: Transit access is limited; driving, rideshare or cycling is easiest for most visitors.
launch-in-indianapolis-holliday-park.need: Trail routes descend into ravines and can be muddy after rain. The Nature Center is closed Sunday even though the outdoor park remains open.

launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.summary: A 1,700-acre urban state park blending wooded ravines, Fall Creek, lakes, military history, paved and natural trails, nature programs, fishing, sledding and picnicking.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.hours: The state park is generally open daily; gate, visitor center, museum, inn and program hours vary. Confirm same-day hours with Indiana DNR.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.parking: Enter from North Post Road and follow signs to the Visitor Center, Delaware Lake, Camp Glenn, Lawrence Creek or other named trailhead. Parking is included after gate admission.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.arrival: Choose Harrison Trace and Delaware Lake for the easiest first visit, Lawrence Creek for a difficult trail, or Camp Glenn for military history.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.restrooms: Restrooms serve the Visitor Center and major picnic and reservable areas; remote trails have limited facilities.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.cost: Current daily vehicle admission is $7 for Indiana plates and $9 for out-of-state plates; pedestrian and bicycle entry is $2 per person age five and older. Other activities may charge.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.accessibility: Parts of the paved 3.2-mile Harrison Trace are wheelchair accessible. Natural trails, creek banks and sledding terrain vary substantially.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed under DNR rules; the dog park requires its own annual membership, application and waiver.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.family: Harrison Trace, Delaware Lake, the Visitor Center, playgrounds and picnic areas are the simplest family combination.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.transit: IndyGo access is limited at the gate; driving is the practical choice for most visitors.
launch-in-indianapolis-fort-harrison-sta.need: The Saddle Barn is temporarily closed for the 2026 recreation season while DNR seeks a new concessionaire. Do not plan trail or pony rides until an official reopening is posted.

launch-in-indianapolis-riverside-regiona.summary: A historic White River regional park being transformed with a 1.5-mile promenade, Adventure Park, nature-themed play, trails, amphitheater, sports and recreation facilities.
launch-in-indianapolis-riverside-regiona.hours: Outdoor park and trail areas are generally available daily. The Family Center is open Monday-Friday 11:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m., Saturday 10:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m., and closed Sunday.
launch-in-indianapolis-riverside-regiona.parking: Free lots and curb access serve the Family Center, amphitheater, sports fields and Adventure Park. Construction may redirect individual approaches.
launch-in-indianapolis-riverside-regiona.arrival: The park spans a long river corridor. Choose Adventure Park north of 30th Street, Taggart Memorial, Family Center, sports fields or the Riverside Promenade first.
launch-in-indianapolis-riverside-regiona.restrooms: The Family Center and developed recreation areas provide facilities during operating hours; trail and construction areas vary.
launch-in-indianapolis-riverside-regiona.cost: Outdoor park, Adventure Park, promenade, playgrounds and trails are free. Golf, programs, rentals and permitted events cost separately.
launch-in-indianapolis-riverside-regiona.accessibility: The new promenade and Adventure Park include modern routes and play features; older fields, river edges and construction zones vary.
launch-in-indianapolis-riverside-regiona.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in ordinary outdoor areas; follow signs around playgrounds, sports fields and construction.
launch-in-indianapolis-riverside-regiona.family: The new Adventure Park playground and trail network are the strongest family draw, with the Family Center as a weather-dependent backup during open hours.
launch-in-indianapolis-riverside-regiona.transit: IndyGo routes and the Central White River Trail connect the park with central Indianapolis.
launch-in-indianapolis-riverside-regiona.need: Riverside is in a multi-phase redevelopment. Verify current access around the Adventure Park, archery project, Taggart playground and any active work zones.

launch-in-indianapolis-broad-ripple-park.summary: A 60-acre White River community destination with a modern Family Center, indoor play, seasonal pool, bark park, playground, courts, fields, woodland and trails.
launch-in-indianapolis-broad-ripple-park.hours: Park grounds are open dawn to dusk. The Family Center is open Monday-Friday 9:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m., Saturday 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m., and closed Sunday.
launch-in-indianapolis-broad-ripple-park.parking: Free park lots serve the Family Center, pool, fields and bark park. Busy pool days and Broad Ripple events can fill spaces.
launch-in-indianapolis-broad-ripple-park.arrival: Use the Family Center for indoor track and play, or route separately to the pool, Bark Park, 10 Acre Woods, playground or river edge.
launch-in-indianapolis-broad-ripple-park.restrooms: The Family Center provides reliable facilities during open hours; pool and outdoor facilities follow seasonal schedules.
launch-in-indianapolis-broad-ripple-park.cost: Outdoor park access is free. Family Center memberships or programs, pool admission, Bark Park access and classes may charge separately.
launch-in-indianapolis-broad-ripple-park.accessibility: The 2023 Family Center and indoor play areas have modern accessible routes; woodland, river and older outdoor surfaces vary.
launch-in-indianapolis-broad-ripple-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in ordinary outdoor areas. The Broad Ripple Bark Park is the designated off-leash area and may require registration or a pass.
launch-in-indianapolis-broad-ripple-park.family: The two-story indoor play structure and indoor track make the Family Center useful beyond good-weather visits; verify entry requirements and program closures.
launch-in-indianapolis-broad-ripple-park.transit: IndyGo buses, neighborhood bikeways and nearby Monon Trail connections provide alternatives to driving.
launch-in-indianapolis-broad-ripple-park.need: The zero-entry pool is seasonal and staffing-dependent. The Family Center is closed Sunday even though outdoor grounds remain open dawn to dusk.

launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.summary: Indianapolis's signature paved rail trail, running from 10th to 96th Street before continuing north through Carmel, Westfield and Sheridan.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.hours: The outdoor trail follows Indy Parks and posted trail hours; use daylight and extra visibility around crossings even when a segment remains legally open later.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.parking: There is no single trail lot. Use designated public parking near 91st, 86th, 75th, 67th, 65th, 62nd, 56th, 54th, 49th, Broad Ripple or connected parks; never block neighborhoods.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.arrival: Choose a segment and turnaround before starting. Downtown, State Fairgrounds, Broad Ripple, Marott Park and 96th Street offer very different experiences.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.restrooms: Facilities are found at connected parks and businesses rather than continuously along the trail; plan a stop before beginning a long route.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.cost: The trail is free. Parking, bike rentals, food and attractions along the route cost separately.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.accessibility: The main asphalt trail is generally 10-15 feet wide and accessible, but street crossings, construction detours and connecting paths vary.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome. Keep leads short, stay right and avoid blocking passing traffic.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.family: Choose a short park-to-park segment and avoid the busiest Broad Ripple periods for young riders. Street crossings still require close supervision.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.transit: Multiple IndyGo routes intersect the trail, and it connects to Fall Creek Greenway, Central Canal Towpath, White River Trail and the Cultural Trail network.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.need: This is an active shared-use transportation corridor. Stay right, announce passes, control speed at crossings, use lights near low visibility and check construction detours before a long trip.
